messages:
maria nguyen: quick async standup — api gw / routing / auth / rl
kevin cho: what I did: wired up new routing predicate for tenant-scoped policies, landed draft config. no prod rollout yet.
sylvia patel: what I did: updated auth middleware to forward x-tenant header, added unit tests.
maria nguyen: blockers: need someone to review the rate-limit rule semantics before we can canary — unsure about burst vs sustained for the new ecommerce traffic pattern
kevin cho: i can review today. quick question: for the generate endpoint, are we using token-based buckets or leaky-bucket per user? current draft uses token-bucket global with tenant tag.
sylvia patel: recommendation: per-tenant token-bucket with a small shared pool fallback. reduces noisy-tenant stomping. see comment on PR.
kevin cho: noted. pinged on PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/542 — @maria nguyen can you add a brief description of expected spike shapes so i can validate the math?
maria nguyen: added a short perf doc in the PR and a sample traffic profile. also pasted a sample config below:
```
routes:
  - path: /v1/generate
    auth: jwt
    routing_policy: tenant_tag
    rate_limit:
      type: token_bucket
      capacity: 120
      refill_per_min: 60
      shared_pool: 30
```
tom b: FYI ran a small local canary against staging with 10% traffic and saw 95p tail go from 180ms -> 320ms when cache misses spiked. logs attached in the PR.
ci-bot: CI: tests passed for PR #542 — 12 checks successful
deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for gateway:v2 -> 10% routes
maria nguyen: plan for today: kevin reviews RL semantics, sylvia to finalize auth fallback, tom to run a 25% canary after fixes; i'll coordinate canary window and monitoring alerts (tracing + 95p latency)
kevin cho: i'll push a small change to switch refill to 90/min and add comments about burst window. will request review from @sylvia patel
sylvia patel: will add integration test for x-tenant header and shared pool behavior. should be done by EOD.
maria nguyen: any objections to rolling canary tomorrow morning 09:30 PT? prefer lower traffic window.
tom b: +1 09:30 PT works for me. i'll reserve observability runbook and be on standby.
maria nguyen: thanks folks — if you hit any blockers drop a note here or ping me directly. :thumbsup:
